name: Chen Wei
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Shenzhen Oriental Fortune Capital (东方富海); chairman of the Shenzhen Venture Capital Association
profile: Chen Wei (陈玮), a Xiamen University accounting PhD and former university lecturer, spent about seven years at Shenzhen Capital Group (rising to president) before founding Oriental Fortune Capital in 2006. The VC firm now manages close to RMB 40bn and has backed 600+ companies (e.g. Kunlun Tech, Jiuxian.com). He remains chairman and an active industry spokesman.
interesting_fact: When the 2008 crisis led LPs to cancel staged commitments, Oriental Fortune's first fund shrank from RMB 900m to under RMB 350m; Chen says he personally borrowed RMB 80m to keep the firm going.
deep_cut_fact: He came to venture capital by accident: in 1999, aged 35 and just back from a visiting-scholar stint in the Netherlands, he wanted to join the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, but the ChiNext board was delayed and hiring frozen, so he applied to Shenzhen Capital instead.
notes: Source of wealth 'Oriental Fortune' = Oriental Fortune Capital (东方富海), not Eastmoney (东方财富). Very public VC figure; frequent speaker at Chinese VC forums. No published press email found; the company website did not load from here. Best route: the firm's official channels.

name: Chai Huijing
profile: Chai Huijing (柴慧京) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List from 2008 to 2018 with real-estate wealth tied to a company listed as 'Guodu' (国都). I could not find any public profile, company page or press coverage to confirm her role or what she is doing now.
notes: Very low public footprint; searches for the exact Chinese name returned nothing relevant. Not the Taiwanese general Chai Hui-chen (柴惠珍). Verify via Chinese corporate registries (Qichacha/Tianyancha) before outreach.

name: Steve Parkin
current_role: Founder and former executive chairman of Clipper Logistics (sold to GXO in 2022); private investor through Knaresborough Investments
profile: Leeds entrepreneur who left school at 16 and founded Clipper Group in 1992. He built it into a listed e-commerce and retail logistics firm (LSE IPO 2014) serving retailers such as John Lewis. GXO Logistics bought Clipper for about £965m in 2022, netting Parkin over £100m in cash plus GXO shares. He now invests privately in Yorkshire businesses.
interesting_fact: Clipper began in 1992 with a single van delivering clothing to fashion stores. Thirty years later it sold for roughly £965m.
deep_cut_fact: In 2017 his private-equity vehicle Knaresborough Investments took a 25% stake in a small Leeds electric-heating business. He likened it to Clipper in its early days.
notes: Not to be confused with David Parkin (Yorkshire business journalist with a Substack). Clipper was a Leeds United sponsor and Parkin is a known Leeds fan. He is also reported to own racehorses, but I could not open a source to confirm it. No published personal or office contact found; Clipper is now part of GXO, so its press office is no longer relevant. Best route is probably Yorkshire business networks.

name: Qian Yunbao
profile: Qian Yunbao (钱云宝) was the controlling shareholder of Hengbao Co. (恒宝股份, SZSE 002104), a smart-card maker in Danyang, Jiangsu, and chairman of Jiangsu Hengshen (carbon fibre). A June 2017 Shenzhen Stock Exchange disclosure records his death on 12 April 2017 and the transfer of his shareholdings by inheritance.
notes: Deceased. Source: Hengbao equity-change report filed with the SZSE, 23 June 2017 (https://disc.static.szse.cn/disc/disk01/finalpage/2017-06-23/2d9ddce9-51ba-4b87-b463-e675958b7fe0.PDF). Not an outreach candidate.

name: Sheng Faqiang
current_role: Co-founder and former chairman, Toread Holdings (探路者); no current executive role found
profile: Sheng Faqiang (盛发强) co-founded Beijing outdoor-gear brand Toread in 1999. In 2009 it listed on ChiNext, where it was called the 'first outdoor stock', and he served as chairman during its mid-2010s diversification. In 2021 the founders transferred control to an investor group led by chip-industry executive Li Ming, and Sheng stepped down as chairman.
interesting_fact: Toread was one of the first companies on Shenzhen's ChiNext growth board when it launched in 2009, and was dubbed China's 'first outdoor stock'.
deep_cut_fact: Before outdoor gear he was in printing: around 1993 he quit a state railway survey-and-design institute, worked as a salesman for a printing plant in Beihai, Guangxi, and then set up his own small printing company.
notes: Since 2021 Toread has been controlled by Li Ming's group, so the company website is no longer a direct route to Sheng. Low recent public profile; I found no personal channels.

name: Sir Angus Grossart
profile: Sir Angus Grossart co-founded the Edinburgh merchant bank Noble Grossart in 1969 and was a leading Scottish arts patron. He died at home in Edinburgh on 13 May 2022 after a short illness. The rich-list entry is shared with his wife, Gay (listed as 'Flure Grossart').
notes: Deceased. Sources: FT obituary 'Angus Grossart, merchant banker, 1937-2022' (https://ftchineselive.com/interactive/71695/en); Glasgow Times tribute, 16 May 2022. The input name 'Sir Angus' is truncated. Not an outreach candidate.

name: Zhang Yichen
current_role: Chairman and CEO, CITIC Capital; Chairman, Trustar Capital; Chairman of McDonald's China master franchise
profile: Zhang Yichen (张懿宸), born 1963 and an MIT graduate, started on Wall Street in 1987 and worked at Bank of Tokyo and Merrill Lynch before joining CITIC Pacific in 2000. He founded CITIC Capital in 2002 and built it into a major China-focused alternative investment firm whose deals include McDonald's China, Alibaba, SF Express and Focus Media. He also chairs Harbin Pharmaceutical and GNC and sits on the HKEX board.
interesting_fact: Through CITIC Capital and Trustar he chairs McDonald's master franchise business in mainland China and Hong Kong, as well as the US supplement chain GNC.
deep_cut_fact: His first Wall Street job, in 1987, was at Greenwich Capital Markets. He later headed proprietary trading at Bank of Tokyo in New York. In a 2014 interview he recommended Charles Duhigg's 'The Power of Habit' and called China's anti-corruption drive 'a colossal exercise in changing habits.'
notes: CITIC Capital's media page directs press enquiries to Corporate Relations (Director: Cindy Tam) at info@citiccapital.com. He is a regular speaker at WEF, Milken and Boao forums, which are good warm contexts for an approach.

name: Neil Ostrer
current_role: Co-founder and Non-Executive Director, Marathon Asset Management (London); retired as European equities portfolio manager in April 2024
profile: Neil Ostrer read history at St Catharine's College, Cambridge, and spent 1981–86 at GT Management. In 1986 he co-founded the London fund house Marathon Asset Management with Jeremy Hosking and William Arah. He ran its European equities until retiring in April 2024 and remains on Marathon's board as a non-executive director.
interesting_fact: Marathon is known for its 'capital cycle' investment approach, which watches how capital flows into and out of industries. It manages tens of billions of dollars, mostly for North American pension funds, endowments and foundations.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding Marathon he worked for GT Management in London and then San Francisco. In 2016 his old college, St Catharine's, Cambridge, elected him a Fellow Commoner.
notes: Not the New York firm of the same name (Bruce Richards). Low personal media profile. Media enquiries for Marathon go to its PR agency, JPES Partners. Marathon also runs an 'Insights & Podcast' section on its site, which could be a natural hook.

name: Mu Jingwei
current_role: Chairwoman, Party Secretary and controlling shareholder, Shanghai Kaibao Pharmaceutical (上海凯宝, SZSE 300039); director of subsidiary Kaibao Xinyi (Xinxiang) Pharmaceutical
profile: Mu Jingwei (穆竟伟, female, born 1979) is a qualified accountant with a Tsinghua EMBA. She controls and chairs Shanghai Kaibao Pharmaceutical, a modern traditional-Chinese-medicine maker best known for Tanreqing injection for respiratory infections. The 'Xinyi Pharmaceuticals' in her rich-list entry is Kaibao's Henan subsidiary. She previously served as Kaibao's deputy GM and board secretary.
interesting_fact: Kaibao's flagship Tanreqing injection is a national strategic reserve drug. In 2024 it was written into China's official treatment protocols for measles, dengue and human avian influenza.
deep_cut_fact: She worked her way up inside the company: Kaibao's 2010 interim report lists her as board secretary. She is now chairwoman, a member of the 14th Shanghai CPPCC, and vice-chair of the Respiratory Drug Research Committee of the China Association of Traditional Chinese Medicine.
notes: The IR email is the board-secretary office address published in Kaibao's 2024 annual report (board secretary: Ren Liwang). Company is in Fengxian, Shanghai. Little English-language coverage of her.

name: Nie Dongsheng
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder (with Yang Yufang), Shenlian Biomedical (申联生物, SSE STAR 688098)
profile: Nie Dongsheng (聂东升, born 1960) spent two decades as a Henan provincial veterinary official before going into business. He has chaired Shanghai-based Shenlian Biomedical since 2006. The company makes veterinary vaccines, notably synthetic-peptide and inactivated vaccines against foot-and-mouth disease in pigs and cattle, and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market. It is now also moving into human biologics through affiliates.
interesting_fact: Shenlian has built its business on synthetic-peptide vaccines for foot-and-mouth disease in pigs, a technology platform rather than the conventional inactivated-virus approach, and it holds national Class-I new veterinary drug certificates.
deep_cut_fact: Before business he was a career veterinary official: section chief at the Henan Veterinary Prevention Station, deputy head of the Henan Animal Quarantine Station, and from 2001 to 2011 head (社长) of the Henan Journal of Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Medicine. He holds the title of agricultural technology extension researcher.
notes: Facts are from Shenlian's 2025 annual report (published April 2026). The IR email is the board office address published there. Low English-language media profile.

name: Liu Shuangguang
current_role: Founder, Chairman (since 2007) and President (since 2019), Gosuncn Technology Group (高新兴, SZSE 300098)
profile: Liu Shuangguang (刘双广, born 1965) is a telecom engineer who founded Guangdong Gosuncn Communication Equipment in Guangzhou in 1997. Today it is Gosuncn Technology Group, a ChiNext-listed maker of IoT products for vehicle networking, smart transport (including railway communications) and public safety. He is the controlling shareholder with about 15% and runs the company as chairman and president.
interesting_fact: Gosuncn has repositioned around connected cars: it builds automotive-grade communication modules and T-Box units with V2X communication, drawing on nearly 30 years of telecoms work.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Gosuncn he was a project-group leader at the Guangzhou Communications Research Institute. He studied communications engineering at Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications and later took an EMBA at Peking University's Guanghua School.
notes: Facts are from Gosuncn's 2025 annual report (April 2026). The IR email is the address published there. Telecom/IoT angle could suit an energy and data-center podcast.

name: Zhang Guifeng
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Fulongma Group (福龙马, formerly Fujian Longma Environmental Sanitation Equipment; SSE 603686)
profile: Zhang Guifeng (张桂丰, born 1963) is a professor-level senior engineer with a Xiamen University EMBA. He spent nearly two decades at the Longyan Tractor Factory and Longma special-vehicle companies in Fujian, then founded Fulongma in 2007. The company makes street sweepers, garbage trucks and other sanitation vehicles and also runs city sanitation services. He chairs the board; day-to-day management has passed to a new president.
interesting_fact: Fulongma's vehicle line-up runs to hundreds of models, including 265 battery-electric models and 28 hydrogen fuel-cell sanitation vehicles. He also championed its 'equipment + services' strategy of running city sanitation operations as well as building the trucks.
deep_cut_fact: He started work in 1984 as a technician in the technical section of the Longma Group's Longyan Tractor Factory, then rose to head of its research institute, chief engineer and deputy GM.
notes: 'Longma Environmental Sanitation Equipment' is now Fulongma Group, based in Longyan, Fujian. Facts are from its 2025 annual report. The electric and hydrogen vehicle line is an energy-transition angle for the podcast.
